items.answer: An immersive experience is a perceived experience through sensory organs that appears real: when a person experiences an environment through sensory organs and fails to distinguish that environment from the person's real environment, perceiving it as the real environment, the technology producing that experience is an immersive technology.

questions.question: In the dictionary sense, what does the term virtual indicate?
options: something is present in essence or effect without being factual
something is present in a computer-generated environment without being factual
something is present in reality or effect without being apparent
something is present in a physical environment without being apparent
questions.explanation: Virtual means being in essence or effect but not in fact. The other options either confuse virtual with reality, computer-generated virtual reality, or ordinary physical presence.

questions.question: Which phrase captures the dictionary sense of reality?
options: the state or quality of being apparent
the state or quality of being artificial
the state or quality of being in essence
the state or quality of being real
questions.explanation: Reality is the state or quality of being real, not merely being in essence, artificial, or apparent. Reality is distinguished from what is merely apparent.

questions.question: In the dictionary definition of virtual reality, what role do sights and sounds have?
options: they play a primary role as user-provided sensory stimuli
they play a primary role as computer-provided sensory stimuli
they play a secondary role as computer-provided sensory stimuli
they play a primary role as real-world sensory stimuli
questions.explanation: In virtual reality, sights and sounds play a primary role and are provided by a computer, possibly along with other sensory stimuli. They are not secondary, user-provided, or drawn from the real world.

data.text: The explanation begins with the dictionary meanings of the two words that make up virtual reality. Those meanings distinguish what is not factual from what is real, and the VR definition describes an artificial environment where computer-provided sights and sounds are primary and user actions partly determine what happens.
points: Virtual means being in essence or effect but not in fact, not attributable to any factual things.
Reality means the state or quality of being real, existing independently of ideas, or actual rather than apparent.
Virtual reality is an artificial environment where computer-provided sights and sounds are primary, and user actions partly determine what happens.

questions.question: What allows a virtual tour that shows real-world imagery to qualify as a VR system?
options: The environment remains a real captured location rather than a synthetic rendered environment
The environment remains a computer-generated scenario rather than a live real environment
The environment remains a live real-time camera view rather than a pre-recorded artificial environment
The environment remains a natural location rather than an artificially presented environment
questions.explanation: A VR system's environment is a computer-generated artificial scenario, even when it is made from real-world imagery or video. A live or unmediated physical setting does not satisfy the artificial-environment requirement.

questions.question: Why is immersion a defining feature of a VR system?
options: It plays a fixed soundtrack into the user's auditory organs
It presents a live camera view to the user's sensory organs
It captures the user's real-world surroundings for the user's sensory organs
It delivers computer-generated stimuli to the user's sensory organs
questions.explanation: Immersive experience in VR comes from computer-generated sensory input reaching the user's senses, not from showing the user's actual surroundings or a fixed media track.

questions.question: What makes user interaction a defining characteristic of a VR system?
options: User actions are recorded without affecting what happens in the environment
User actions happen separately from what changes in the environment
User actions are limited to following a fixed path in the environment
User actions partially determine what happens in the environment
questions.explanation: A VR system must be interactive: the user can act on elements and the user's actions must partly shape the environment's dynamic changes. Fixed watching, logging, or disconnected actions do not satisfy this requirement.

data.text: Virtual reality is identified by the combination of an artificial environment, sensory experience, and user interaction. The environment is a computer-generated world, not a real environment, even when it uses real imagery or video. Sensory stimuli and user interaction make that environment immersive and interactive, which distinguishes a virtual reality system from other systems.
points: A virtual reality system is defined by an artificial environment, sensory experience, and user interaction.
A virtual reality artificial environment is a computer-generated world, not real, even using real imagery or video.
A virtual reality system gives computer-generated stimuli to the user's sensory organs, immersing the user in the artificial environment.
A virtual reality system is interactive: user actions partially determine what happens, causing dynamic changes in the environment.

questions.question: Why is a computer-aided design system not a virtual reality system?
options: It lacks a real-time view because it keeps the user in the real room
It lacks interaction because it keeps the user in the real room
It lacks an immersive experience because it keeps the user in the real room
It lacks a virtual environment because it keeps the user in the real room
questions.explanation: A CAD system provides a virtual environment and allows interaction, but the user still sees the real world around the screen, so the experience is not immersive. Missing only that one characteristic is enough for it not to be VR.

questions.question: Why is a video conferencing system not a virtual reality system?
options: It lacks interaction and an immersive experience because it shows a real place in real time through a screen
It lacks a virtual environment and an immersive experience because it shows a synthetic place in real time through a screen
It lacks a virtual environment and an immersive experience because it shows a real place in real time through a screen
It lacks a virtual environment and interaction because it shows a real place in real time through a screen
questions.explanation: Video conferencing is interactive, but it presents a real-world environment in real time through a screen, so it is neither a virtual environment nor an immersive VR experience. The third option misdescribes the system, because the scene shown is real, not synthetic.

questions.question: Why is a three-dimensional movie experience not a virtual reality system?
options: It lacks a virtual environment because the viewer only watches the film
It lacks interaction because the viewer only watches the film
It lacks a real-world view because the viewer only watches the film
It lacks an immersive experience because the viewer only watches the film
questions.explanation: A 3D movie can provide a virtual environment and a partly immersive experience, but the viewer cannot change what is displayed, so the system is not interactive. The other options misidentify the missing VR characteristic.

data.text: A system must have a virtual environment, sensory immersion, and interaction to be a VR system; missing any one characteristic makes it non-VR. Applying that test, computer-aided design, video conferencing, and 3D movie systems are classified as non-VR. Each fails for a different reason: computer-aided design lacks sensory immersion, video conferencing presents a real environment through a screen without sensory immersion, and 3D movies are non-interactive.
points: A system is a virtual reality (VR) system only if it has a virtual environment, sensory immersion, and interaction.
A computer-aided design system is not VR because it lacks sensory immersion, while it provides a virtual environment and interaction.
A video conferencing system is not VR because it shows a real environment through a screen and lacks sensory immersion.
A 3D movie experience is not VR because it lacks interaction: viewers only watch and cannot change content.

questions.question: Why does a virtual tour that recreates a real world using real-world imagery or video still count as a virtual reality system?
questions.reference_answer: It still counts because it is a computer-generated scenario rather than the actual environment. The artificial environment is a computer-generated representation of a real or imaginary world, even when real-world imagery or video is used. Changes in that scenario are not happening in real time, so it remains a virtual environment.

questions.question: Why is a computer-aided design system not a virtual reality system even though it supports a virtual environment and interaction?
questions.reference_answer: A computer-aided design system fails the immersive-experience requirement. An immersive experience is one in which a person cannot distinguish the experienced environment from the real environment, but in a computer-aided design system the user sees the real world around the computer screen while using a mouse. A virtual reality system requires a virtual environment, immersive sensory experience, and interaction together.

questions.question: Why is a video conferencing system not a virtual reality system even though it is interactive?
questions.reference_answer: It is not a virtual environment and not an immersive experience. A video conferencing system presents a real-world environment in real time through a screen, so the user remains in the real world and the screen only aids interaction. A virtual reality system requires an artificial virtual environment, immersive sensory experience, and interaction, so failing any one excludes it.

questions.question: Why is a three-dimensional movie experience not a virtual reality system even though it provides a virtual environment and a partly immersive experience?
questions.reference_answer: It lacks the required user interaction. The viewer only watches and cannot change the displayed content, so user actions do not partially determine what happens in the environment. A virtual reality system requires a virtual environment, immersive sensory experience, and interaction, and user interaction produces dynamic changes in the artificial environment.
